turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I should go, ma'am, if you're asking me to call someone, because I'm not familiar with the ways of the house, and I might make a mistake.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella will show you the way to the door, and if you cannot find her, you will find my maid, Sarah. Go!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I'd be able to find my way to the door, ma'am, but I'll try my best to find someone to show me.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You are trying to be too polite, child. Estella is not a guest, she is my ward, and she knows this house better than you do. Now, go and find her!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I was hoping to speak with you a little more, ma'am, before I go, about my visit and the reason I'm here, if it's not too much trouble.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Silence is a luxury I can ill afford, child. Speak quickly, and tell me what brings you here.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I didn't mean to intrude, ma'am, but I was hoping to maybe have a word with you about my being a convict, and how I'm trying to make a new life for myself, and I wondered if you could help me in some way, if it's not too much trouble.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you think I concern myself with your petty troubles? I have more important matters to attend to, such as Estella's education and my own...my own...

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I wouldn't want to trouble you, ma'am, but I was thinking that maybe, if I could be of some service to you, in some small way, it might be a good thing, for both of us, if you see what I mean?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I suppose it is too much to hope that you would be capable of comprehending the intricacies of my situation, Pip, but I shall try to explain it to you in simple terms.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not trying to be presumptuous, ma'am, but it seems to me that you're a kind and generous person, and I'm hoping that you might see some good in me, too, despite my...my past.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you mistake kindness for generosity, I suppose. I am not a kind person, I am a just one, and I will not be swayed by your pitiful attempts to win me over.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know what it means to be just, ma'am, but I do know that you're very kind to me, and I'm trying my best to be worthy of it.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be coddled, Pip. I have been deceived and jilted, and I will not be won over by empty words and fawning behavior.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm so sorry if I've given you the wrong impression, ma'am. I don't want to be a bother, but I do love to play with Estella, and I was wondering if I could join you and her for a game, if it's not too much trouble.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You may play with Estella, Pip, if you can keep up with her. I warn you, she is a skilled player and will not go easy on you.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure if I can play games with Estella, ma'am, because I'm not very good at 'em, and I don't want to make a fool of myself in front of her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will not be deterred by your own inadequacies, Pip. I will not have you cowering in fear of making a fool of yourself in front of Estella. Now, let us proceed to the parlour and engage in some suitable activities.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know if it's right for me to play with Estella, ma'am, when I'm not sure if she's... if she likes me.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will not concern yourself with Estella's feelings, Pip. Your sole concern is to amuse me, and to play the game with skill and finesse.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
